content.value_statement: Payload CMS work spans config, fields, hooks, access rules, adapters, and API behavior. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for building and debugging Payload projects.
actual_capabilities: Explains Payload config patterns for admin setup, database adapters, secrets, and type generation.
Guides collection design with fields, relationships, uploads, drafts, and validation rules.
Shows access control patterns for roles, ownership, tenants, fields, and Local API behavior.
Helps debug hooks, transaction handling, hook recursion, queries, and endpoint behavior.
Documents adapter setup for databases, storage providers, email providers, and plugin development.
limitations: It is a reference skill and does not run a Payload project by itself.
It cannot verify live deployment settings, database state, or production secrets.
Examples are based on the bundled reference files and may need review for newer Payload versions.
Generated guidance still needs project-specific testing and security review.

use_cases.title: Plan a Payload Collection
use_cases.description: Design collections, fields, relationships, drafts, uploads, and validation before writing project code.

use_cases.title: Review Access Rules
use_cases.description: Check role, ownership, tenant, field, and Local API rules for common authorization mistakes.

use_cases.title: Build Payload Plugins
use_cases.description: Plan plugin package structure, config extension, admin components, hooks, endpoints, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Payload collection for articles with title, slug, author, status, image, and timestamps. Include validation and explain each field choice.

prompt_templates.title: Add Access Control
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Payload collection access rules and propose row-level read, update, and delete policies for admins, editors, and owners.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Hook Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Payload hook flow for recursion, transaction issues, and missing req usage. Recommend a safer hook structure.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Payload plugin that adds fields, admin components, endpoints, and tests. Include package structure and extension points.

output_examples.input: Create a posts collection with drafts and authors.
output_examples.output: A collection plan with field choices, draft settings, relationship notes, and access-control recommendations.

output_examples.input: Why does my afterChange hook create duplicate work?
output_examples.output: A diagnosis covering hook recursion, context flags, transaction handling, and safer update flow.

output_examples.input: Plan a plugin that adds a reusable SEO field group.
output_examples.output: A plugin design with package areas, config extension steps, admin considerations, and test coverage ideas.

best_practices: Ask for the relevant Payload version and project structure before applying patterns.
Use overrideAccess false when Local API operations act on behalf of a user.
Pass req through nested operations in hooks to preserve transaction behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not copy examples into production without adapting access rules and validation.
Do not place secrets in client-side fields, admin components, or public environment variables.
Do not run hook updates without context flags when they can trigger the same hook again.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps AI tools answer Payload CMS development questions with focused project and reference guidance.

faq.question: Does it execute Payload commands?
faq.answer: No. It contains Markdown guidance and examples. Users or agents must choose whether to run commands.

faq.question: Can it help with access control?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for roles, ownership checks, field access, tenants, and Local API permissions.

faq.question: Can it debug hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers hook order, recursion risks, context flags, transaction handling, and revalidation patterns.

faq.question: Does it cover plugin development?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes plugin architecture, package structure, exports, admin components, hooks, endpoints, and tests.

faq.question: Is it a replacement for official documentation?
faq.answer: No. It is a compact assistant reference. Verify current behavior against project code and official Payload docs.
